chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

Leaning towards this world despite what you see of it, is folly, and lagging behind in good deeds when you are convinced of good reward for them is obvious loss, while trusting in every one before trying is weakness.

key_terms.الرُّكُونُ: Leaning or settling comfortably (often implying complacency)

ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of spiritual weakness according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this maxim from *Nahj al-Balagha*, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) delineates the triad of spiritual negligence: mistaking worldly attachment for security is *jahil* (folly), assuming reward without effort is *ghabn* (a deceptive loss), and premature trust is *ajz* (inability). This teaching reflects the Shia emphasis on *tawassum* (discernment) and active vigilance (*yaqdhah*) as prerequisites for true spiritual maturity, warning against passive reliance on divine mercy without corresponding human effort.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 384. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:

Leaning towards this world despite what you see of it, is folly, and lagging behind in good deeds when you are convinced of good reward for them is obvious loss, while trusting in every one before trying is weakness.
